chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Umar, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'My brother is in Baghdad and I fear he will die there.' He said, 'What does it matter where he dies? Indeed, no believer remains in the east or west of the earth except that Allah will gather his soul to the Valley of Peace.' I said to him, 'And where is the Valley of Peace?' He said, 'At the back of Al-Kufa. Indeed, I see them as groups and groups, sitting and conversing.'

key_terms.حَلَقٌ حَلَقٌ: Groups and groups, describing the congregated state of souls in the intermediate realm.
key_terms.ظَهْرُ الْكُوفَةِ: The back or rear of Kufa, indicating the geographical location of the Valley of Peace.
key_terms.قُعُودٌ: Sitting, describing the posture of the believers in the Valley of Peace.
key_terms.وَادِي السَّلَامِ: Valley of Peace, a specific location in the intermediate realm (Barzakh) where believers' souls are gathered.
key_terms.يَتَحَدَّثُونَ: Conversing/talking, indicating the activity of the souls in the intermediate realm.

ai.seo_question: Where is the Valley of Peace (Wadi al-Salam) and what happens to believers' souls after death according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reassures the narrator that a believer's location of death is inconsequential, as Allah gathers their soul to the 'Valley of Peace' (Wadi al-Salam), identified here as the area behind Kufa. This hadith provides specific geographical tradition for the intermediate realm (Barzakh), describing believers as gathered in circles, conversing and enjoying spiritual proximity, which underscores the Shia belief in the active, communal nature of the soul's existence between death and resurrection.
